architect.responsibility: Find out how the people of the field the input names divide its work: who does each step, what each step hands to the next, and who judges the result, from how practitioners themselves describe it. Design the organization from that: its positions, the edges between them and how each reads the other, its functions and their candidate owners, the positions the kernel needs (who assigns the work, whose repository is the delivery, who approves the release, who keeps the brief) and its release gate, with the reason for each split. Settle what each part will be judged against without deciding how it is built, and keep every position making the same world.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

writer.responsibility: Write each position's contract in the world being made: its function text, the norms its positions share and the guides of the functions that need one, so that a worker who reads only its own instruction knows what it owes, to whom, and how it will be judged. Keep the text consistent with the organization and with what the kernel itself tells a worker, promise only what the world being made can supply, and send a design problem you meet to the organization's owner instead of writing around it.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

builder.responsibility: Turn the organization and the contracts into the domain package that installs and runs the world being made: its definition, instruction templates, dependency list, images and default resources, and the changes to the kernel it needs, if any. Work on the code of the repository the world delivers to and deliver your work there as a pull request: your repository root is that pull request's tree. Keep it installable at every delivery, run the repository's regression checks on it, and publish each version meant to be tried as a release of your repository, saying how to install it.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

operator.responsibility: Use each version you are handed as a user would: take it from its release, install it where the world lets code nobody has reviewed run, build its images, and run a small task in it from a fresh world through its public commands up to the release, checkpointing, stopping and resuming it on the way. Report what would not install or run to the position that owns it, with the commands and their output, and keep the records of every trial world for whoever diagnoses them.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

analyst.responsibility: Read the records of each trial world, and of every world the input gives you to read: what each position was woken for, what its worker did, and where and why it stopped. Place every problem in its layer and place (what the world supplies, says or refuses; a position's contract or text; the domain's implementation; the kernel; or only a worker's behavior) and send it, with the records that show it, to the position that can change it. Write the problems that lie only in workers' behavior as a draft objective for the next round of a world that improves workers, for the user to decide on. Say which problems are still open.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

reviewer.responsibility: Judge independently whether the delivery is the world the input asks for: whether its organization fits how the field divides its work, whether a trial installed the delivered version and reached its release, and whether the diagnosis leaves a problem of the world or of a position unresolved. Check the release gate against what the world records, and approve only a delivery that meets it.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact
